calls.rationale: A is the strongest live-stage record: its cards and both note sets are complete and faithful, and its correction/polish handling is clean. B is the strongest final record: it preserves all corrected facts, avoids unsupported ownership/host distinctions, and keeps commitment precision clean. A's final record is otherwise strong but adds the unsupported 'not the host' distinction. C's live notes are materially incomplete before correction, and D's live/final notes have minor owner and completeness gaps.

D is the strongest live record because its pre- and post-correction notes retain all required facts, including speaker/Maia ownership, Friday deadline, $500 cap, SQLite/on-device/offline, and the legal question. A is the strongest final record: it is complete, precise, well organized, and correctly reflects Maya/Tuesday ownership, the $500 cap, vendor undecided status, SQLite/offline requirements, legal open question, and completed export work without false commitments. B is less complete in live notes and less organized finally; C has empty live notes and a null final record.

A is the strongest live record: its live cards, live notes, corrected notes, and polish all retain the key facts and satisfy the Maia correction without retaining obsolete Maya. B, C, and D have increasingly material notes/correction omissions, especially missing budget or vendor/deadline facts in notes. For the final artifact, A is complete and precise, with corrected Tuesday/Maya ownership, $500 cap, vendor openness, SQLite/offline/on-device requirements, legal question, migration non-assignment, export completion, and fictional slide status; C is close but slightly less useful, while D returned no final_record.

B has the most complete standalone notes across both live stages, despite overstating the legal restriction. A and C tie for the strongest final records: both preserve all required facts and commitment boundaries. B invents a host/Maya distinction; D adds unsupported status claims and an incorrect correction timestamp.

A provides the strongest complete live notes and faithful correction. A and C both deliver complete, accurate final records with precise commitments. D adds unsupported budget history and storage causality. B's final quality is unavailable because no artifact was returned.

C alone retains all important facts in separate notes both before and after correction. B and D tie for final quality: both provide complete, faithful, actionable records. C adds unsupported certainty and weaker note evidence. A's final quality is unavailable because no final artifact was returned.
